lead: Valencia treasures four UNESCO recognitions: a 15th-century Gothic monument, a thousand-year-old institution of justice, the most explosive festival in the Mediterranean and a unique language of sound.

UNESCO recognises the outstanding universal value of Valencia’s heritage with four listings spanning two centuries of history: from the jewel of civil Gothic that is La Lonja de la Seda to the most recent recognition, the manual ringing of bells, in 2022. Three of them are intangible heritage – living traditions you can witness on any visit – and one is a monument that can be visited all year round.
The Valencian Community also has seven other World Heritage sites, including the Palm Grove of Elche, the Misteri d’Elx and the Festa d’Algemesí.

items.title: La Lonja de la Seda (Silk Exchange)
items.subtitle: A jewel of civil Gothic and a symbol of merchant power
items.body: Declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site on 5 December 1996, La Lonja de la Seda is one of the most representative examples of 15th-century European civil Gothic. The slender helical columns of the Contract Hall, the gargoyles of the Orange Tree Courtyard and the palm trees that touch the ceiling of its “paradise” make it an architectural jewel without equal. Two decades after its listing, UNESCO also made Valencia part of the Silk Roads, which link another 32 cities in Asia and Europe.
facts: Every day of the year from 9:30 to 19:00 · Free admission with the València Tourist Card
notes: The Columned Hall, where trade deals were sealed, is decorated with a Latin inscription warning merchants to act with honesty. The spiral columns have no direct precedent in Valencian Gothic architecture.

items.title: The Water Tribunal
items.subtitle: The oldest functioning court of justice in Europe
items.body: Every Thursday of the year, at twelve noon, one of Europe’s most singular traditions takes place beneath the Door of the Apostles of Valencia Cathedral. The Water Tribunal of the Valencian Huerta, with roots in Roman times, publicly and orally settles disputes between farmers over the use of irrigation water. In 2009 UNESCO declared it an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity for its unique character, its thousand-year effectiveness and its living role in Valencian society.
facts: Door of the Apostles · Valencia Cathedral
Every Thursday at 12:00 · Open to all · Suspended on public holidays and between Christmas and Epiphany
notes: The tribunal sits with no written minutes and no lawyers: the syndics of the eight historic irrigation canals (acequias) deliberate and pass sentence in Valencian within minutes. In centuries of operation, none of its rulings has been appealed before an ordinary court.

items.title: Las Fallas de Valencia
items.subtitle: The most creative and explosive festival in the Mediterranean
items.body: Las Fallas is the celebration where the plastic arts, music, pyrotechnics, gastronomy and the art of living come together. Ephemeral monuments up to several storeys high, built by falla artists over months, are raised in every neighbourhood of the city only to burn on the night of 19 March in the Cremà. UNESCO declared Las Fallas an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2016 as a festival unique in the world, with no equivalent in any other culture.
facts: From 15 to 19 March · Free admission to most events · The Cremà is on the night of the 19th
notes: On the last Sunday of February, the fallera mayor proclaims the official start of Las Fallas from the Serranos Towers in the event known as La Cridà. The mascletàs, musical gunpowder explosions, thunder through the Plaza del Ayuntamiento every midday in March.

items.title: Manual Bell Ringing
items.subtitle: A living language of sound high up in the Miguelete
items.body: In 2022 UNESCO declared Spanish manual bell ringing an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. In Valencia, professional bell ringers keep this language of sound alive in several of the city’s churches – Campanar, Santos Juanes and the Cathedral itself – using different swinging and pealing techniques to call the community together on major festivals. The Miguelete houses one of the largest collections of Gothic bells in Spain: eleven bells, including two weighing more than 1,700 kilos and the oldest in the Crown of Aragon, dating from 1305.
facts: Miguelete · Cathedral · Campanar Church · Santos Juanes
Visit to the Miguelete with bell ringing · Limited to 25 people · Advance booking required
notes: The ringing can reach 120 decibels, but it is exempt from volume restrictions because of its status as an Intangible Asset of Cultural Interest. No bell ringer has suffered hearing loss, thanks to the traditional positioning technique.

items.title: Rock Art of the Mediterranean Basin
items.body: Prehistoric cave paintings spread across many municipalities of the Valencian Community.

items.title: Palm Grove of Elche
items.body: The largest palm grove in Europe, with more than 200,000 palm trees in the urban area of Elche.

items.title: The Misteri d’Elx
items.body: A medieval liturgical drama in two acts performed every August in the Basilica of Santa María in Elche.

items.title: Festa de la Mare de Déu de la Salut in Algemesí
items.body: A celebration with muixeranga, dolçaina and tabalet that dates back to the 13th century in the town of Algemesí.

items.title: The Tamboradas
items.body: Ritual drumming from Alzira and l’Alcora that marks the start of Holy Week.

items.title: Dry-Stone Wall Building
items.body: A traditional technique shared with Croatia, France, Greece, Italy and other European countries.

items.title: La Maderada
items.body: The tradition of transporting timber down rivers on rafts, a multinational nomination with other European countries.

blocks.title: Practical information for experiencing UNESCO heritage
items: La Lonja de la Seda is open every day from 9:30 to 19:00
The Water Tribunal sits every Thursday at 12:00 at the Cathedral
Las Fallas take place from 15 to 19 March every year
Bell ringing at the Miguelete requires advance booking – maximum 25 people
The València Tourist Card includes free admission to La Lonja de la Seda
The Water Tribunal does not sit on public holidays or between Christmas and Epiphany
